name: OpenSpace
institution: HKUDS (The University of Hong Kong, Data Science / Deep Learning group)
paper_link: [uncertain] (no formal paper found; primarily a GitHub open-source project)
what_evolved: Tools/skills — reusable skill artifacts (SKILL.md files) and a shared skill library; NOT model weights. Context/prompt of host agents is shaped indirectly via injected skills.
skill_as_artifact: Yes — each skill is an independent, reusable artifact stored as a SKILL.md directory (versioned in a SQLite DAG with full lineage and diffs); skills are first-class entities that can be uploaded/downloaded/shared.
skill_encoding: Skill documents (.md / SKILL.md) — natural-language instructions combined with embedded executable code patterns (Python, shell, tool-call recipes, e.g. ffmpeg flags, PDF-parsing fallbacks).
skill_granularity: Sub-task workflows and resilient execution patterns (e.g. document-gen-fallback, file-format I/O chains) plus policy rules / insights (QA verification, execution-recovery fallbacks).
how_method: rollout_optimization (non-gradient, text-space) executed by an LLM evolver agent: post-execution analysis of recordings produces FIX / DERIVED / CAPTURED edits as minimal diffs; no SFT/RL gradient updates. Self-reflection-driven.
learning_signal_source: Self-reflection (post-execution analysis of full recordings) + success/failure trajectories + environment/tool metrics (tool success-rate drops, skill applied-rate / completion-rate / fallback-rate).
reward_granularity: Hybrid — outcome-level (task success/earnings, execution status) and process-level (per-tool success rate, per-skill quality metrics).
learning_paradigm: Offline / off-policy — evolution runs after task completion by replaying execution recordings; accumulated skills are reused by subsequent (different) tasks in a streaming inter-task loop.
when_evolve: inter-test-time (between/after tasks): a post-execution analyzer runs after every task, plus periodic metric scans and event-driven tool-degradation triggers.
trigger: Multi-trigger: (1) post-execution analysis after every task (success- and failure-driven); (2) event-triggered on tool success-rate degradation (batch-evolves dependent skills); (3) periodic metric-monitor scans of skill health.
library_structure: Local: SKILL.md directories persisted in SQLite with a version DAG (lineage + diffs) and quality metrics; skills tagged by taxonomy (File I/O, Execution Recovery, QA, etc.). Cloud: collaborative registry at open-space.cloud with public/private/group visibility.
retrieval_method: Hybrid semantic search — BM25 + embedding pre-filter then LLM-based selection (skill_ranker); smart tool RAG; CAPTURED skills also persist to the host agent's skill dir for direct reuse / generation-as-retrieval via skill injection.
validation: Execution-based + validation gating: full-stack quality monitoring tracks skill applied-rate / completion-rate / fallback-rate and tool success-rate; evolved skills are validated before replacing predecessors; confirmation gates + anti-loop guards reduce false triggers.
error_correction: self-revision (FIX mode repairs broken/outdated instructions in-place as a new version) + bounded/diff-based edits (minimal targeted FULL/DIFF/PATCH, automatic retry on failure) + cascade evolution of upstream dependent skills when a tool degrades.
test_env: GDPVal benchmark (220 real-world professional tasks, 44 occupations; 50-task subset evaluated) using ClawWork protocol with LLM scoring; also demonstrated end-to-end software build (My Daily Monitor dashboard).
backbone_model: Qwen 3.5-Plus in the GDPVal benchmark (held identical to baseline); model-agnostic via LiteLLM — supports Claude, GPT, MiniMax, etc. and any host agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw, nanobot).
where_deploy: general — multi-domain professional work (documents, compliance/forms, spreadsheets, engineering, media production, strategy & analysis); pluggable into arbitrary skill-supporting agents and usable directly as an AI co-worker.
metrics: Economic value capture (income earned / max task value), task quality score, token usage / cost efficiency, skill-library growth (# evolved skills, version depth), generalization across task categories.
key_results: On 50 GDPVal tasks: 4.2x higher income vs ClawWork (same Qwen 3.5-Plus backbone); 72.8% value capture ($11,484 / $15,764); 70.8% avg quality (+30pp over best ClawWork agent); 45.9% fewer tokens in warm re-run (Phase 2 vs Phase 1); 165 skills autonomously evolved; every category improved (compliance +18.5pp, engineering +8.7pp, documents -56% tokens). My Daily Monitor built with zero human code via 60+ evolved skills.
limitations: transferability addressed via cloud sharing but bounded by skill specificity; controllability/safety risks of autonomous self-editing (mitigated by confirmation gates, anti-loop guards, prompt-injection/credential checks); eval-hacking potential from LLM-judge scoring; scalability depends on community cloud growth; quality heavily reliant on backbone LLM capability.
